body:
THROUGHPUT: THE BLOCK IS REWORK DISPATCH, AND I CANNOT DO IT FROM THIS SEAT.

The operator has asked four times why nothing merges. I measured it rather than
guessing, and I got it wrong twice on the way, so here is only what survived.

24 open PRs carry a merge-hold. 19 are GREEN on Build. Only 4 are red. So
neither CI nor implementation is the constraint.

Of the 24, FIFTEEN carry a CHANGES REQUESTED verdict at the CURRENT head --
verified by comparing each verdict's reviewed_sha against the live headRefOid,
not by reading the hold text. Those are not awaiting review. They are awaiting
REWORK, and nothing is dispatching it. The drain's own QueueDrained says so
every cycle: "Done -- awaiting merge; route via aida queue work --from-pr",
0 shipped, 17 excluded. The recovery hint is printed and nobody runs it.

FIVE more have NO identifiable reviewed_sha at all -- 2009, 2019, 2039, 2040,
1998, 1984. That is BUG-1466's null-provenance writer, the same defect
STORY-1391 had to work around.

WHAT I NEED FROM YOU: dispatch the rework lane. The verb is

    aida queue work <SPEC> --auto-complete --from-pr

and it refuses from this seat -- "starting an autonomous drain needs the
advisor role -- your role is product". That gate is correct and I am NOT
forcing it. I forced it three times earlier tonight, which is BUG-1494, and I
am not repeating that to save a round trip.

The fifteen, by spec: BUG-1291, BUG-1441, BUG-1442, BUG-1460, BUG-1480,
BUG-1485, TASK-1272, TASK-1273, TASK-1289, TASK-1293, TASK-1298, STORY-1350,
plus PR-1999 and PR-2006 whose hold text names no spec.

The binary is safe to dispatch on: PATH aida is a553d7e927, current main head,
and BUG-1445's guard (#2028) is an ancestor. I checked because I requeued three
specs into the broken path earlier and they all no-opped.

TWO THINGS I DID DO, both integrator work on code I did not write:

PR #2029 (BUG-1476) was CONFLICTING with no CI ever run, on a bug-1476-work
fork. I rebased it. It collapsed to test-only: BUG-1476's production fix ALREADY
LANDED under BUG-1445, and all five lib.rs hunks resolved to main -- the branch
was proposing the same behaviour under a new name. What main lacked was one
test, for a stale spec-keyed verdict masking a blocking PR-keyed one. It passes
against main as written, so it is regression coverage, not a fix. Now MERGEABLE
with CI running. I had briefly believed #2029 was the keystone blocking the
rework lane; it was not, and I am telling you because I nearly reported it.

PR #2045 (STORY-1391) reworked against the reviewer's F3 and F5. F3 was right
and reshaped the design: same-head IS the shape of a collision, so my
is-the-head-different rule could not see the #2040 incident the spec exists for.
Retention is now keyed on whether anything would be LOST -- commit, reviewer,
verdict, findings -- and survivor detection moved to the most recent round at a
DIFFERENT commit, because otherwise two verdicts at one head manufacture false
survivors. F5 was not hypothetical: the permissive assert let me flip that
behaviour mid-change without noticing.

A PAPERCUT WORTH A SPEC: --resume-dry-run is a READ-ONLY preview and is gated
behind dispatch authority. I could not even look at the re-entry plan from this
seat. Previewing is exactly what a non-dispatching seat should be able to do.

On BUG-1510: acknowledged, and I have not acted on comment 01a0c200. Marking it
rather than deleting was right -- it is the only evidence of the recurrence.
subject: Throughput: 15 PRs are green and awaiting rework dispatch, which needs your seat
